keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «바다의 그 많은 소금은 어디서 올까?(질문)» 와 «강이 소금을 계속 실어 오지만 물만 떠나기 때문에 바다는 짜다(답)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the question (where does all the salt come from?) and the answer (the ocean is salty because rivers keep bringing salt in, but only water leaves). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.qen: Where does the salt come from?
boxes.a: Rain breaks down rocks, and rivers carry salt to the sea

boxes.qen: Why must you not drink seawater?
boxes.a: It makes you thirstier, so sailors carry fresh water

qs.q: Why would drinking seawater make you thirstier?
qs.qko: 바닷물을 마시면 오히려 더 목이 마른 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: Because your body would need even more water to get rid of the salt
Because seawater is too cold to drink
Because seawater has no minerals in it
evs: Seawater is so salty that your body would need even more water to get rid of the salt, so you would become thirstier.
You are thirsty, and you are surrounded by water.
Rivers carry these minerals, including salt, all the way to the sea.
That is why sailors carry fresh water on long trips.
why: 바닷물은 너무 짜서 몸이 소금을 없애려면 물이 더 필요하고, 그래서 더 목이 마르게 된다고 했어요.
Seawater is so salty that your body would need even more water to get rid of the salt, so you would become thirstier.

qs.q: In "but the salt stays behind," what does "stays behind" mean?
qs.qko: «but the salt stays behind» 에서 «stays behind» 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: remains in the same place when something else leaves
evs: In the ocean, the sun heats the water until it evaporates, or turns into gas, but the salt stays behind.
Much of it comes from rocks on land.
The answer is that river water holds only a tiny amount of salt and keeps flowing.
That is why sailors carry fresh water on long trips.
why: 물은 증발해서 기체로 떠나지만 소금은 «남는다» 고 했어요. «stays behind» 는 다른 것이 떠나도 그 자리에 남는다는 뜻이에요.
The water evaporates and leaves as gas, but the salt «stays behind», which means it remains where it is.

qs.q: How does salt from rocks on land get into the sea?
qs.qko: 땅 위 암석의 소금은 어떻게 바다로 들어가나요?
opts: Rain breaks down rocks and picks up minerals, and rivers carry them to the sea
Fish carry rocks from the land into the sea
The wind blows salt from the sky into the water
evs: Rainwater is slightly acidic, so it slowly breaks down rocks and picks up tiny bits of minerals.
But you must not drink it.
Rivers carry these minerals, including salt, all the way to the sea.
After millions of years, the salt has built up until about 3.5 percent of seawater's weight is salt.
why: 약한 산성인 빗물이 암석을 부수며 광물을 모으고, 강이 소금을 포함한 이 광물을 바다까지 실어 간다고 했어요. 두 문장을 이어야 해요.
Slightly acidic rainwater breaks down rocks and picks up minerals, and rivers carry these minerals, including salt, to the sea. You need both sentences.

ends: Why is the Dead Sea so salty that people can float on it?
사해는 왜 사람이 둥둥 뜰 만큼 짤까요?
How do people make salt from seawater?
